first_impression.reaction: Typed 'marriage licence' on the train. First line answers it straight away: Australia doesn't have one, you give a notice to a celebrant 1 to 18 months out. It's dated November 2026, so yes, it's current. The first sentence is very long on a phone screen, though, and the whole thing is about Australia. I'm in Singapore, so the bits that actually apply to me are the NZ, Hawaii and 'other destinations' sections. Key Takeaways are good. Bookmark, not enquiry.

journey.quote: If you are searching for a marriage licence in Australia, there is none to apply for.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first line. Exactly what I want.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, you [give a notice of intended marriage to an authorised marriage celebrant](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/marriage/get-married) at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding, you marry before that celebrant and 2 witnesses, and the celebrant sends the paperwork to the state or territory registry, which registers the marriage.
journey.reaction: Good info, but it's one huge sentence. On my phone that's half the screen. I had to read it twice.

journey.quote: Marry abroad and the destination's law takes over, and some places do issue licences.
journey.reaction: OK, so it's not only Australia. Gives me a reason to keep scrolling.

journey.quote: A licence permits a marriage while a certificate records one, and in Australia the certificate that counts is the official copy from the state or territory registry, not the ceremonial one signed on the day.
journey.reaction: Didn't know the pretty one wasn't the real one. That's a screenshot.

journey.quote: "I call upon the persons here present to witness that I, A.B. (or C.D.), take thee, C.D. (or A.B.), to be my lawful wedded wife (or husband, or spouse)", or words to that effect.
journey.reaction: Interesting, but I asked how to get a licence, not what to say at the altar. Scrolled past.

journey.quote: You [apply for a copy of your official marriage certificate](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/marriage/get-married) from the registry, and your celebrant can do this on your behalf, generally at a cost.
journey.reaction: 'At a cost.' How much? Just tell me how much it costs, or at least where to check.

journey.quote: Arrange it at least 3 working days before the wedding; it expires after 3 months.
journey.reaction: Real numbers. This is the part that actually applies to me as a non-Australian.

journey.quote: There are no state residence or US citizenship requirements, and our [Hawaii wedding guide](/destination-weddings/getting-married-in-hawaii) sets out the timeline.
journey.reaction: Clear, and a link if I want more. I'd tap that.

journey.quote: For anywhere else, ask the destination's embassy or consulate what you will need.
journey.reaction: Fair, but that's where I fall. Nothing for Singapore or anywhere in Asia. I'd have to search again.

journey.quote: What is recognised is the marriage, not the licence.
journey.reaction: Short, direct, matches what I'd type into Google. FAQ is good.

journey.section: Plan your wedding abroad with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Whichever country makes it legal, one Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD, so it's an Australian company. 'Your time zone' is nice, but I came for a definition, not a planner.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how much does the official registry certificate cost, or where do I check the current fee? (page says 'generally at a cost')
Is there a cost to lodge the Notice of Intended Marriage itself?
How long after the wedding until I can actually get the official certificate in hand?
Does any of this apply if neither of us is Australian, e.g. we live in Singapore but want to marry in Australia?
How much are the New Zealand and Hawaii licence fees?
Does Wedded Wonderland work with couples who don't live in Australia? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Concierge fee worked out? (page only says it is agreed in writing; deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: As at November 2026, you [give a notice of intended marriage to an authorised marriage celebrant](https://www.ag.gov.au/families-and-marriage/marriage/get-married) at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding, you marry before that celebrant and 2 witnesses, and the celebrant sends the paperwork to the state or territory registry, which registers the marriage.
turn_offs_found.why: The answer is there, but packed into one long sentence. On a phone it reads as a wall. The Key Takeaways say it more simply.

turn_offs_found.quote: Under [section 46 of the Marriage Act](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ma196185/s46.html), a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination must say, in the presence of the witnesses, words that include: "Marriage, according to law in Australia, is the union of 2 people to the exclusion of all others, voluntarily entered into for life."
turn_offs_found.why: A whole section of quoted legal wording sits between the notice and the certificate parts. It isn't what a 'marriage licence' searcher asked, and it's more scrolling before the licence vs certificate answer.

turn_offs_found.quote: and your celebrant can do this on your behalf, generally at a cost.
turn_offs_found.why: Cost is my first follow-up question and the page waves at it without a figure or a pointer to where the fee is listed.

would_share_with: My partner: a screenshot of the Key Takeaways, especially the ceremonial vs official certificate point

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your date, your guest list and where you would like to marry, and begin with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=marriage-licence&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I got my answer and I don't know this brand. It quotes in AUD and is written for Australians, and I'm nowhere near choosing a planner. I'd tap the Hawaii or NZ guide link before this.
